Harbor District Council Meeting Notes
The Harbor District Council met to discuss seawall repair and parking meters. The council approved a $4.2 million contract for seawall repair, which will start in March and take 14 months. The fish market's relocation plan during closures remains unresolved.
The north section of the seawall is 61 years old and has cracks along 340 meters. "The north section of the seawall is 61 years old and the engineering survey found cracks along roughly 340 meters of it."
The recommended bid for seawall repair is $4.2 million from Coastline Civil. "Recommended bid is from Coastline Civil at $4.2 million, which was the lowest of three bids."
The seawall repair will start in March and take 14 months, with two closures of three weeks each. "Work would start in March and take about 14 months. Fenn said the boardwalk would stay open except for two closures of about three weeks each."
The capital reserve will be left with about $600,000 after the seawall repair. "Fenn said the capital reserve would be left with about $600k."

Alder Creek Library Book Budget Strategies
The Alder Creek branch library serves 9,000 people with a $41,000 book budget. They spend 38% on ebooks and audiobooks, up from 22% five years ago. The library joined a regional sharing group to cut costs.
The Alder Creek branch library spends 38% of its book budget on ebooks and audiobooks. "Its director, Rosa Delgado, said the branch now spends 38 percent of that budget on ebooks and audiobooks, up from 22 percent five years ago."
Digital titles cost the library more than print titles. "Digital titles cost the branch more than print. A popular new novel that costs $28 in hardcover can cost the library $55 for an ebook license that expires after 24 months or 26 checkouts, whichever comes first."
The regional sharing group reduced average hold times on bestsellers from 31 days to 12 days. "Delgado said the group cut average hold times on bestsellers from 31 days to 12 days."
